definitions: A large tent, typically canvas or vinyl stretched over a network of center poles and guy-wires, that serves as the primary performance venue for a traveling circus, engineered to shelter thousands of spectators and a full three-ring program under a single peaked roof.
colloq. A tent so ambitious it needs its own zip code and a dedicated crew just to raise the center pole.
example: The circus crew spent six hours raising the big top, a canvas dome so thiccc it could have sheltered the entire county fair underneath it.
etymology: Circus operators in 19th-century America began calling their main performance tent the big top by the 1890s, distinguishing it from the smaller sideshow and menagerie tents around it. The name was never subtle. Neither was the tent.
caption: A canvas big top stands fully raised under open sky, its center poles straining against guy-wires pulled taut around the perimeter.
